summary:
CI-GATE-PROOF-DO-NOT-MERGE Builds engineering organizations with the confidence that comes from applying a strong yet simple discipline based on understanding the real need, designing for the people who have to operate it, and making ownership explicit enough to survive without direct oversight. Designs so that no individual is structurally required, treating a key-person dependency as a defect to engineer out rather than a strength to celebrate. It is a habit built over more than two decades, from individual contribution through technical leadership to running organizations.

Leads multidisciplinary engineering organizations, working alongside matrixed product partners, and has instituted the governance an AI-augmented engineering practice needs to run safely in production. Strongest when building: new products, new markets, new business lines, understood and mapped before committing to them, with organizations built to hold up under scrutiny from regulators, boards, and eventual acquirers.

Decides on evidence over opinion in architecture calls, vendor decisions and technical direction, and writes the reasoning down clearly enough that someone else can follow it without a meeting. Applies that same evidentiary gate to self-originated proposals first. Treats communication as a quality mechanism rather than announcement, on the view that a standard nobody is aware of effectively does not exist and that alignment decays without deliberate repetition.

As a people leader, starts from a people-first perspective, approachable and patient, a steady listener who lets the team own its goals and its wins. Stays curious, hungry for growth, and guided by getting it right as fundamentally more important than being right. The through-line runs from hands-on engineering to enterprise architecture, cloud modernization, and VP-level leadership, across regulated industries where mistakes reach patients, regulators, or the budget.

experience.title: Vice President, Software Engineering
bullets: ## Role Progression
Promoted three times in three years, advancing from Director of Product Development to Senior Director of Software Engineering to Vice President, Software Engineering.
## AI-First Organizational Transformation

Championed enterprise AI adoption against initial executive resistance-instituting the organization's AI-augmented SDLC and delivering a documented 3-4x increase in meaningful code output (500K -> 1.5-2M lines) with 30%+ productivity improvement. Conceived and led the organization's first AI Hackathon, designed the AI Development Framework (Developer Directs -> AI Executes -> Developer Validates), and created the AI-Native PDLC-a 5-stage framework feeding curated context to both engineers and AI agents.

Built an AI Governance Architecture satisfying HIPAA-adjacent compliance: usage policies, security guardrails, cost governance, and audit protocols-converting ad-hoc experiments into governed, repeatable pipelines across the full SDLC. Defined the security rails with security stakeholders early in adoption, so AI surfaces and remediates previously invisible weaknesses and leaves the security posture materially stronger than before.

Scaled adoption from individual developer productivity to an agent-multiplied delivery model-multiple agents per engineer, automated LLM-based PR review against guardrails with human review reserved for what falls out, and unit-of-work cost governance keeping AI economics rational at scale.

That governance now underpins production agentic products-an AI clinical scribe, in use across 1,000+ clinics, 1,600+ providers, and 300+ practices, and an agentic patient assistant, in use across 2,000+ clinics and by 200k+ patients-embedding agentic workflows directly into the customer experience. An automated insurance-matching agent is still piloting at 100+ clinics rather than in general release.
## Organizational Scale & Team Operations

Helped shape the engineering strategy for a board-sponsored Global Capability Center initiative-framing it as a long-term engineering capability build rather than a cost-arbitrage play, with a phased rollout, standards calibrated to market rather than lowered, and onboarding engineered for scale. Program ownership and final design authority remained outside the role.

Built and leads a direct engineering organization of 70-100 across seven teams (software engineering, quality engineering, DevOps, platform) with six direct reports and product partners matrixed alongside-inside a PE-backed, market-leading healthcare SaaS serving 5,000+ locations. Direct P&L accountability for $4.8M in strategic investments within a $23M R&D budget, delivering 35%+ efficiency improvement.

Helped steer the strategy for a maturing core market: rationalizing legacy investment, refocusing growth capacity on new products, new markets, and partnership-driven revenue, and standing up new business lines that redistributed the organization around them.

Established a DevOps center of excellence and consolidated DevOps leadership to convert expert-held knowledge into documented, standardized, shared practice-explicitly to eliminate single-person dependency.
## M&A Integration & Operational Transformation

Led post-acquisition integration of an acquired healthcare platform engineering team, building small-shop delivery up to enterprise-grade operating standards through documented CI/CD maturity, quality gates, and compliance remediation, established methodically rather than mandated overnight. Continues to support M&A activity, including on-site walk-the-wall integration work for an India-based RCM workflow acquisition.

Converted recurring operational escalations into an executive operating-model transformation discussion-reframing isolated support conflicts as systemic ownership, escalation, key-person dependency, and product-health investment issues across Engineering, Operations, Product, and executive stakeholders.
## Platform Modernization & Engineering Reliability

Led a multi-year transformation of architecture from review-oriented advisory activity into an accountable technical leadership capability-clarifying boundaries between architects, Staff Engineers, managers, and delivery teams while emphasizing delivery enablement, distributed ownership, microservices and distributed-systems modernization alignment, and measurable outcomes.

Stood up the Platform Initiative-repositioning architecture from mercenary advisory into an engine of delivery: reusable components, patterns, services, cross-cutting layers, and the knowledge, documentation, and standards teams build on, delivered in part through surgical nearshore engagements.

Led engineering for a Healthcare SaaS platform serving 5,000+ urgent care providers; coached and guided the creation of the Architecture Hub (repo-based compliance scoring across security, reliability, maintainability, deployability, observability); shaped reliability strategy that eliminated critical latency failure modes and championed Jenkins -> CircleCI migration completed in one day with zero incidents. Builds the rails before accelerating-testing, safeguards, and rollback capability first-then defaults to rolling forward rather than reflexively reverting, and removes gates that have become ritual rather than protection.
## Organizational Leadership & Strategic Operations

Shifted engineering culture from ticket-taking to value-delivery engineers who partner with product on the why, right-size the grain of effort, and carry accountability for outcomes-a shift funded by AI-driven efficiency gains.

Designed quarterly leadership onsites with a progressive maturity arc (Identity to Excellence to Focus to Growth to Recalibration to Sharpen the Standard), a deliberately paced, multi-quarter build rather than a single training event. Served as technical ambassador to PE stakeholders, backing engineering decisions with data rather than opinion, with eventual exit scrutiny in mind. Championed people-first culture under financial constraint, advocating retention cases against committee pushback with documented evidence of individual contribution, while maintaining top 10% performance outcomes.

Leads AI adoption from the front, personally evaluating and using the tooling before institutionalizing policy, and staying directly engaged with the engineering, the details, and customers rather than managing through layers and summaries. Measures adoption by an ambition test-it is working when commitments get bigger, not merely when the same work finishes faster.

Treats AI as a magnifier of whatever an organization already is, shaping the human organization deliberately by consolidating effort onto fewer things done well, co-locating accountability and authority, and making ownership explicit, so multiplied speed compounds instead of fragmenting into local optimizations and duplicated dysfunction.

Diagnosed and intervened on a misaligned hiring chain-recruiters, job descriptions, interviewers, and engineering expectations each encoding a different standard-instituting consistent competency frameworks, structured assessment for disputed candidates, and explicit guardrails against title inflation and referral-driven hiring.

strategicInitiatives.summary: Diagnosed and intervened on a misaligned hiring chain-recruiters, job descriptions, interviewers, and engineering expectations each encoding a different standard-instituting consistent competency frameworks and guardrails against title inflation and referral-driven hiring.
strategicInitiatives.narrative: Hiring quality was inconsistent, and the diagnosis was that each link of the chain encoded a different standard: recruiters screened against one bar, job descriptions described another, interviewers applied a third, and engineering expected a fourth. leadershipFrameworks.name: AI Development Framework
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Developer Directs -> AI Executes -> Developer Validates
leadershipFrameworks.description: The operating model that shifted the engineering organization from manual code production to agent-augmented review. Engineers provide context, intent, and architectural direction; AI agents generate first-draft code, PR descriptions, test cases, and documentation; engineers validate, refine, and own the output. The bottleneck moves from build capacity to review quality-a fundamentally better constraint. Four core principles: Provide Blueprints, Iterate in Cycles, Delegate Systematics, Shift Your Skills. Underpinned by a stated hierarchy: coding is an implementation activity, while software engineering is the understanding of systems, constraints, tradeoffs, and outcomes. As code production commoditizes, judgment, understanding, and communication remain the differentiators, and the engineer's job becomes guiding both people and tools.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Designed from practitioner experience-personally evaluated AI tooling before institutionalizing as governance policy. Documented as an interactive infographic with data visualizations showing the 80/20 oversight shift.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Definition Pipeline (BMAD Lineage)
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Idea -> Refinement -> PRD -> TRD -> Plan -> Tasks
leadershipFrameworks.description: The intake half of the AI-augmented SDLC. Started from BMAD-an agentic lifecycle where specialized agents handle Analyst, PM, Architect, Scrum Master, Developer, and QA phases-and adapted rather than adopted wholesale into a homegrown definition chain: an idea is developed, refined, turned into a PRD, then static technical artifacts (TRDs), then a plan, then tasks. Context engineering ensures each stage produces artifacts that serve both human reviewers and downstream agents.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: BMAD evaluated as an early reference model, then evolved with the chief architect and staff engineers into the organization's own pipeline-proven on real delivery, refined through team feedback.

leadershipFrameworks.name: A-D-V-R Cycle - AI Hackathon Workflow
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Architect -> Direct -> Validate -> Repeat
leadershipFrameworks.description: A high-speed iterative workflow designed for the organization's first-ever AI Hackathon. Positions the developer as Architect and the AI as Apprentice. Each cycle: provide a precise small task from the blueprint, AI generates the output, developer validates and approves before the next cycle begins. Emphasizes that the developer's value shifts from typing speed to clarity of architectural thinking.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Created for and deployed during the first AI Hackathon-a cultural transformation event conceived and led to shift the organization from AI skepticism to embedded practice.

leadershipFrameworks.name: AI-Native Product Development Lifecycle
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Signal -> Context -> Decision -> Execution -> Memory
leadershipFrameworks.description: A 5-stage PDLC that treats AI agents as first-class participants alongside human engineers. Each stage produces curated context packets consumed by both humans and AI coding agents. Addresses the structural insight that AI has made implementation cheap-shifting the true organizational constraint to product definition quality. Includes the Cold-Read Validation method proving artifact quality before build begins.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Created and piloted through a structured 2-day onsite proving session with the product and engineering teams. 69% Day 1 readiness score validated the framework's practicality.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Architecture as Delivery Enablement
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Guardrails - Distributed Ownership - Outcome Accountability
leadershipFrameworks.description: A model that reframes architecture from centralized review or detached advice into an accountable technical leadership capability. Architecture reduces friction, creates reusable patterns, clarifies decision rights, enables modernization, and gives teams guardrails so they can make good decisions independently.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Developed through multi-year coaching, executive influence, role-boundary clarification, and the Architecture Hub assessment model across a complex regulated software portfolio.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Security Design & IP Protection Framework
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Tiered Access - Context Boundaries - Audit Protocols
leadershipFrameworks.description: A structured approach to securing AI-augmented engineering workflows in regulated environments. Defines tiered contractor security models, establishes context boundaries for AI tooling (what data AI agents can and cannot access), and implements audit protocols satisfying HIPAA-adjacent compliance requirements. Security rails are defined with security stakeholders early, and AI's tendency to expose previously invisible weaknesses is treated as the first honest accounting of risk-so the posture ends materially lower-risk than before adoption.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Designed to address the organizational risk concerns that initially blocked AI adoption-turning security from a blocker into an enabler through governance architecture.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Operating Model Transformation
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Ownership - Escalation - Support - Product Health
leadershipFrameworks.description: A systems-thinking approach for converting recurring escalations into executive-level organizational design work. Identifies ownership ambiguity, operational noise, support capability gaps, key-person dependency, and product-health opportunity cost; then reframes the conversation from incident response to sustainable operating mechanisms.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Developed through cross-functional coaching and executive influence in a regulated, post-acquisition platform environment where historical expectations outlived the operating model.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Leadership Maturation Arc
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Identity -> Excellence -> Focus -> Growth -> Recalibration -> Sharpen
leadershipFrameworks.description: A deliberate multi-quarter progression designed for an engineering leadership team. Each quarter's theme builds intentionally on the last-producing artifacts, operating models, and shared language that compound over time. The arc treats leadership development as a designed system, not a series of disconnected offsite events.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Designed and facilitated across six consecutive quarterly leadership onsites, each building on the artifacts of the last.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Agentic Architecture Discipline
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Definition-First, Then Iteration
leadershipFrameworks.description: Before recommending any agentic approach, evaluate the cost-to-value ratio against the specific use case. Avoid architectural trend-following. The principle: definition precedes iteration. Surfaces the insight that the real bottleneck in AI-augmented engineering is often product definition quality-not build capacity-and ensures AI investments deliver genuine leverage rather than novelty.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Developed through practitioner evaluation of AI tooling patterns; applied across integration and product transformation initiatives.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Value Delivery Engineering
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Why Before What - Right Grain - Skin in the Game
leadershipFrameworks.description: The cultural operating model that converts ticket-takers into value-delivery engineers. Engineers partner with product to understand objectives before scoping, keep effort at the right grain (no over-engineering, no under-delivery), and carry accountability for outcomes. AI-driven efficiency funds the shift: freed capacity goes to judgment, partnership, and ownership.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Developed as AI lifted raw production capacity and the constraint moved from building to judgment-structured through team design, messaging, and knowledge-transfer clinics.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Agent-Multiplied Delivery Model
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: One Engineer - Many Agents - Guardrailed Review
leadershipFrameworks.description: The delivery model that multiplies one contributor's impact across multiple agents: agentic coding, automated LLM-based PR review against guardrails, and human review concentrated on what the automated gates surface. Quality is built into the pipeline, and the whole model runs an explicit refinement loop-learn, integrate, ship a better version of the process.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Evolved from individual developer productivity (Copilot-era) through chief architect and staff/principal engineer partnership into the organization's standard delivery practice.

leadershipFrameworks.name: AI Unit Economics Framework
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Model Selection - Token Economics - Unit-of-Work Cost
leadershipFrameworks.description: Cost governance for AI at scale: model selection and internal benchmarking, token and fine-tuning economics, unit-of-work cost tracking for product-embedded AI, and scale-path evaluation (including self-hosting) that accounts for first- and second-order consequences-control, IP protection, maintenance burden, and obsolescence risk.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Built on the observation that AI costs can outrun AI value without discipline-practitioner evaluation of models and platforms turned into an organizational decision framework.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Platform Initiative
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Reusable Components - Patterns - Knowledge - Standards
leadershipFrameworks.description: Architecture repositioned from mercenary advisory into an engine of delivery: reusable components, artifacts, tooling, patterns, services, and appropriate layering of cross-cutting concerns-alongside the knowledge, documentation, and standards that make reuse stick. Progression is deliberately rational: no boiling the ocean.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Stood up by repositioning the architecture function, anchoring it with senior technical hires, and directing surgical nearshore engagements against specific platform objectives.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Say-Do Operating System
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Big Rocks -> Committed Dates -> Say-Do Ratio
leadershipFrameworks.description: A lightweight initiative-tracking cadence for leadership work: a small set of big rocks, meaningful start and committed dates, and a say-do ratio that tests whether leaders select worthy initiatives, protect focus, surface blockers, and carry commitments to completion. Positioned as a team tool for shared accountability and support, not a private status report. Paired with a standing evidentiary gate: a proposal is not ready when it is persuasive, only when it is evidenced-problem, friction, benefits, risks, mitigation, and return-with logs and demonstrated steps expected before an escalation, and the same standard applied upward and to the leader's own initiatives.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Built from the engineering leadership team's weekly operating cadence: planned, active, paused, and blocked work made visible, aging work questioned, low-conviction items removed.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Engineering Maturity & Accountability Manifest
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Kill Your Heroes, Stop Doing It Harder
leadershipFrameworks.description: A written leadership standard separating role-appropriate execution from leadership-level impact. Redirects heroic intervention toward surfacing and fixing systemic gaps: clearer performance calibration, direct conversations, accountability for each team's part in outcomes, and patience for investments that build durable capability rather than only protecting the current sprint. The same standard generalizes beyond its origin: across the wider organization, key-person dependency is treated as a defect to be designed out, whether it shows up in operational knowledge or in a role that has become load-bearing alone.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Codified with the engineering leadership team in February 2026 out of an acquired platform's hero-dependency recovery; external constraints treated as real without becoming an excuse for avoiding ownership.

leadershipFrameworks.name: AI-Era Leadership Platform
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Leadership Over Management - Practice Over Mandate - Whole-System Ownership
leadershipFrameworks.description: Six convictions for leading through generational change: transformational leadership over administrative management, because the routine mechanics of management can be automated and the human work cannot; leading AI adoption by personal use before mandate; sitting with uncertainty without losing direction; owning the whole system including the parts that hurt; flatter organizations concentrated in fewer, stronger leaders; and practitioner depth as leverage a leader never graduates away from.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Owner's stated leadership philosophy, carried in the executive summary and lived through the operating model, AI adoption, and role design at Experity.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Engineering Operating Model
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Exploration - Improvement - Industrialization
leadershipFrameworks.description: One operating model with three delivery modes matched to the type of work: exploration validates fast and light, improvement tightens feedback loops on what already works, and industrialization scales what is proven with real rigor. Underneath all three sit WIP limits, small batches, dependency reduction as a design goal, SLO-driven prioritization, and DORA-grounded delivery. Architecture acts as a force multiplier-paved roads, reference implementations, decision records-and AI governance is built into the model rather than bolted on.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Designed and directed within the engineering leadership team. Organization-wide implementation and measured gains are not yet confirmed.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Staff Engineer / TSAL Model
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: One accountable technical leader - defined ramp - explicit boundaries
leadershipFrameworks.description: A defined role, not a title bump: hands-on, single-accountable technical leadership spanning architecture and delivery, with explicit scope boundaries-product partnership, technical roadmap, cross-functional coordination, contractor leadership, PR quality, standards, and mentorship-and a ramp plan built into onboarding rather than assumed. Applied with the same shape in two separate product areas. The philosophy underneath: senior technical roles multiply the organization; they do not absorb whatever breaks.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Applied consistently in two separate product areas. Organization-wide standardization is not confirmed.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Nine-Pillar Well-Architected Framework
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Nine pillars for a regulated healthcare platform
leadershipFrameworks.description: A Well-Architected standard built for the healthcare context instead of a generic cloud checklist: security with HIPAA as a design input, reliability by design, performance against real usage, operations as part of architecture, cost at design time, maintainability for the team that inherits the code, testability as a design property, scalability before growth forces it, and extensibility from the start. Designed as a shared vocabulary for technical decisions and to plug into self-service assessment-application-level grading, risk scoring, required artifacts-so architecture visibility scales without a central bottleneck.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Designed and directed with the architecture team, developed with engineering-wide input. Final pillar definitions and production rollout were named as next steps.

leadershipFrameworks.name: Leadership Operating Principles
leadershipFrameworks.tagline: Structure Over Heroics - Evidence Over Assertion - Repetition Over Announcement
leadershipFrameworks.description: A consistent operating philosophy expressed the same way whether the subject is hiring, architecture, a departure, or a security policy. Three principles carry the weight. No individual should be structurally required, so a key-person dependency is engineered out rather than celebrated. Nothing advances on assertion: proposals state problem, friction, benefits, risks, mitigation, and return, and the gate is applied to self-authored proposals before anyone else's. Communication is a quality mechanism, because a standard nobody is aware of effectively does not exist and alignment decays without deliberate repetition.
leadershipFrameworks.origin: Drawn from day-to-day work with senior engineering managers and technical leaders, and from a standing engineering-leadership forum.

That hands-on depth, built over more than a decade of lead-developer and architect roles, is what makes the leadership judgment that follows it trustworthy: building the team, the operating cadence, and the technical-lead structure a system needs once it has traction.
